findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the pipeline encoding with ADR 0123 §5: either state in the plan (and amend the ADR) that pipeline attestations leave out the `engine:` line on purpose to stay byte-identical, or write `engine: pipeline` on new pipeline attestations as the ADR describes.
evidence: ADR 0123 §5: "The signed plan-review attestation gains an `engine` field (`\"pipeline\"` or `\"agentic\"`) inside the signed payload ... A missing field reads as `\"pipeline\"`: every attestation signed before this change keeps validating"
Leaf: "appends `engine: <name>` when the verdict's `coverage.engine` is set and is not `\"pipeline\"`. A pipeline manifest is byte-identical to today's"
Parent AC 1 names the ADR as the record of 'engine provenance in the attestation', so the ADR is part of the parent's contract.
findings.finding: The leaf changes the shape of the signed field that ADR 0123 §5 defines (the ADR is the parent's own recorded decision on how the attestation records the engine). The ADR says the attestation 'gains an `engine` field ("pipeline" or "agentic")', and only attestations signed before the change lack it. The leaf never writes `engine: pipeline`: new pipeline attestations also leave the line out, so they are byte-identical to today's. The meaning is the same, since absence reads as pipeline and the signature still covers whether the line is there. But the leaf neither mentions this departure nor updates the ADR, so the ADR and the code will describe different formats. Divergence kind: incomplete_enumeration (a wording/encoding mismatch, not a contract break).
scenarios: A later auditor or tool written to ADR 0123 §5 expects every post-change attestation to carry `engine:`. It treats a new pipeline attestation as pre-change (or as missing the field), when it is really a current pipeline attestation.

findings.finding: The drift-refresh carry-forward makes a pipeline-engine probe re-sign an agentic verdict and stamp it `engine: agentic`. refresh_attestation's only caller is orchestrator.drift_refresh, which runs only when `engine == "pipeline"` (__init__.py:561) and probes with pipeline criteria (orchestrator.py:499-506). drift_refresh_candidate (attest.py:230-263) accepts any valid attestation without checking its engine. The new field records which engine produced the attestation, but here the re-certification decision is made by the pipeline engine. This is the same cross-engine replay that ADR 0123 already bars for idempotent reuse, verdict reuse and drift refresh as 'shortcuts that reuse or re-sign a PIPELINE attestation' (__init__.py:542-543; reuse.py:229-232). Now that the engine is readable from the signed manifest, the better mechanism is to gate the candidate on it, not to carry it forward.

An auditor comparing the engines counts this as an agentic certification even though no agentic review judged the drifted code.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] In `build_manifest`, emit `engine:` only when `coverage.engine` is in the closed set {"agentic"} (anything else is treated as pipeline or rejected). In `manifest_engine`, map unrecognised recorded values to a defined fallback, so status always matches the schema enum.

Plan: schema property is `"pipeline"`, `"agentic"` or null
findings.finding: build_manifest is specified to write `engine: <name>` for any `coverage.engine` value other than 'pipeline', with no check against the known engines. On the sign-review path that value comes from the stored sidecar payload (resign.py:170 `coverage = payload.get("coverage") or {}`), not from `resolve_plan_review_engine`. A malformed or edited sidecar value would be signed into the attestation. `manifest_engine` would then return it, and `plan_review_status` would emit a value outside the schema's planned enum (`"pipeline"`, `"agentic"` or null), so the MCP schema validation the plan tests would fail. A value with an embedded newline or `dep ` text could also forge an extra manifest line inside the signed bytes.
scenarios: A hand-edited or corrupted sidecar has `coverage.engine: "agentic\ndep <hash> x"` or `"floor"`. sign-review re-signs it, then `review-plan --status` / MCP `plan_review_status` returns an engine value that fails the schema enum, or the manifest gains a forged extra line.
findings.suggested_fix: Define a closed set such as `_KNOWN_ENGINES = ("pipeline", "agentic")` in manifest.py (it must not import the package __init__, per manifest.py:6-8). In build_manifest, `if engine in _KNOWN_ENGINES and engine != "pipeline": lines.append(f"engine: {engine}")`. In manifest_engine, return the recorded value only if it is in `_KNOWN_ENGINES`, else "pipeline". Add a unit test for an unknown or multi-line engine value.
